source_text: Hinc explicata patientia Dei, et dispensatione mitissima, qua non vult mortem morientis, nisi ut revertatur et vivat, approbare quod dixerat etiam per exempla persistit, facitque mentionem eorum, qui in terra chananaea viventes pessime iram Omnipotentis accenderant, ut impenderetur ultione iustissima Israelitarum triumphis, sub Dei iam lege viventium. Illos enim antiquos habitatores sanctae tuae terrae odiens, quoniam odibilia opera tibi faciebant, per medicamina et sacrificia iniusta, et necatores filiorum sine misericordia, voluisti perdere per manus parentum nostrorum, ut dignam percipiant peregrinationem puerorum Dei, quae tibi omnium charior est terra [n195] . Septem gentes, quibus ex maxima parte deletis, Israelitis terra repromissionis data est, propter quid Deus voluerit perire, testatur. Ne enim in una hominum natura per aliquam personarum acceptionem apud Deum videretur esse discretio; propter quid Chananaei meruerint interfici, commendat. Illos ergo antiquos habitatores sanctae tuae terrae, inquit, odio habuisti. Quamobrem? Certe secundum te debuit subdere, quia de diabolica erant commixtione generati, quia a tenebrarum principe possidebantur, quia tabificavit Adam omnes de sua stirpe venturos. Verum nihil horum: sed quam causam reddit odiorum? Sola opera commissa per voluntatem liberam. Oderas, inquit, eos, quoniam exosa tibi opera faciebant. Verum ne nesciremus, quae essent opera, tuque haec gentium facta concupiscentiam genitalem vocares, ipsas species operationis exsequitur. Per medicamina, inquit, et sacrificia iniusta, et necatores erant filiorum sine misericordia; id est, maleficiis et sacrificiis serviebant, quae iniusta erant, cum idolis offerebantur, cultu Creatoris abiecto; quibus sacrilegiis ipsas necessitudines deputabant; daemonas videlicet etiam parricidiorum immanitate placantes. Vide itaque quam non de eo loquatur crimine, quod confingit Manichaeus, id est, cunctis per naturam adhaerente mortalibus, qui hinc illos potissimum offendisse commemorat, quod nec a parvulorum suorum exitiis temperabant. Quorum certe mors non recurreret ad interfectoris invidiam, si propter unum peccatum et parricida Deo displiceret, et filius.
pass_a_gloss: From here, the patience of God having been explained, and the mildest dispensation by which he does not want the death of the one dying except that he may return and live, he persists in approving what he had said even through examples, and he makes mention of those who living most evilly in the Canaanite land had kindled the wrath of the Almighty, so that it might be expended by a most just vengeance for the triumphs of the Israelites, now living under God's law. For those ancient inhabitants of your holy land, hating them, because they were doing works hateful to you, through medicines and unjust sacrifices, and killers of sons without mercy, you wanted to destroy through the hands of our parents, that the children of God may receive a worthy sojourning, which land is dearer to you than all. He testifies on account of what God wanted the seven nations to perish, of whom the land of promise was given to the Israelites, they having been destroyed for the most part. For lest in one nature of humans a discretion might seem to be with God through some acceptance of persons; he commends on account of what the Canaanites deserved to be killed. Those therefore ancient inhabitants of your holy land, he says, you held in hatred. For what reason? Certainly according to you he ought to have subjoined, because they were generated from a diabolical mingling, because they were possessed by the prince of darkness, because Adam wasted all about to come from his stock. But none of these: but what cause of hatreds does he render? Only works committed through a free will. You hated them, he says, because they were doing works hateful to you. But lest we not know what the works were, and you would call these deeds of the nations genital desire, he follows the very species of the operation. Through medicines, he says, and unjust sacrifices, and they were killers of sons without mercy; that is, they were serving malefices and sacrifices, which were unjust when they were offered to idols, the cult of the Creator having been thrown off; to which sacrileges they were assigning even their own kin; placating demons namely even by the monstrosity of parricides. See therefore how he does not speak of that charge which Manichaeus invents, that is, clinging to all mortals through nature, who commemorates that they especially offended from this, that they did not even abstain from the destructions of their own little ones. Whose death certainly would not run back to the spite of the killer, if on account of one sin both the parricide displeased God, and the son.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Having explained God’s patience and his most gentle ordering of things, by which he does not desire the death of the dying person but rather that he turn back and live (compare Ezekiel 18:32; 33:11), the writer continues to prove what he said by examples. He mentions those whose terribly wicked lives in the land of Canaan had kindled the Almighty’s anger, so that the land would be granted, through the most just punishment, to the victories of the Israelites, now living under God’s law. “Hating those ancient inhabitants of your holy land, because they did hateful deeds before you through spells and unjust sacrifices, and were merciless killers of children, you willed to destroy them through our fathers’ hands, so that the land dearest to you of all lands might receive a worthy settlement of God’s children” (Wisdom 12:3–7).

He testifies why God wished the seven nations to perish, after whose destruction for the most part the promised land was given to the Israelites (compare Deuteronomy 7:1–2). Lest God appear to distinguish persons by partiality within one human nature, he explains why the Canaanites deserved to be killed. “You hated,” he says, “those ancient inhabitants of your holy land.” Why? According to you, he should certainly have added: because they were generated from a devilish union; because the ruler of darkness possessed them; because Adam infected everyone who would come from his stock. But he says none of these things. What reason does he give for the hatred? Only deeds committed through free will. “You hated them,” he says, “because they did deeds hateful to you.”

But so that we would not be ignorant of the deeds, and so that you could not call these acts of the nations reproductive desire, he details the kinds of action themselves. “Through spells,” he says, “and unjust sacrifices; and they were merciless killers of children.” That is, they served sorcery and sacrifices that were unjust because they were offered to idols, after worship of the Creator had been abandoned. To these sacrileges they devoted their own relatives, appeasing demons even by the enormity of murdering their children. See, then, how far he is from speaking of the crime Manichaeus invents, a crime naturally adhering to every mortal. He recalls that their chief offense was that they did not refrain even from destroying their own little children. Those children’s deaths would not bring odium on the killer if both the murderer and the child displeased God because of one and the same sin.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
